transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-02
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Marcus (Redwood SE), Emily (Oakwood Head of Data), Raj (Oakwood CTO), Sofia (Oakwood Security Lead)

Summary:
Quick onboarding kickoff for Oakwood Health to align on implementation plan, security/compliance requirements, pilot scope and timelines. Covered SSO/SSO, VPC/private deployment options, SOC2/KMS expectations, and immediate next steps to start a small pilot.

Topics:
- Onboarding checklist and timelines
- Deployment modes (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC)
- Security/compliance: PHI, SOC 2, KMS, audit logs
- Networking and VPC peering, firewall rules, egress
- Pilot success criteria and evaluation metrics

Transcript:
00:00 Jared: Hey everyone good afternoon thanks for joining, we really appreciate you carving out the time for the kickoff. I think Priya's got the agenda and we'll run through the overall plan and then Marcus will take the tech bits, cool?
00:08 Priya: Hi hi, yep thank you — uh Emily Raj Sofia thanks for coming. Quick note on agenda: onboarding checklist, security questions, pilot scope and timeline, action items. If anything else please interrupt.
00:20 Emily: Thanks, excited to get started. We want a tight pilot window, ideally 3 weeks of integration + 4 weeks evaluation. Primary use case is clinical note summarization and triage support — some PHI likely in the dataset.
00:32 Raj: Quick context, we run on AWS — EKS clusters, some data in RDS, and a little S3 staging. We're leaning toward a private deployment because of PHI but open to Redwood Dedicated if isolation and KMS are available.
00:46 Marcus: Yeah that makes sense. We'll go over Dedicated vs Private. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity on our infra with tenant isolation and logs, while Private (VPC) is customer-controlled networking — you manage the VPC peering and we deliver an appliance or control plane depending on config.
01:05 Sofia: On encryption, we need to know if Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and if audit logs include per-request token-level metadata for compliance. Also retention windows — can you TTL logs for PHI?
01:20 Marcus: Short answer: yes on customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; Dedicated also supports integrations with cloud KMS in many cases. Audit logs are available via the Console and you can configure retention; for PHI we usually recommend Private with your KMS so keys never leave your account.
01:35 Raj: Is there a SOC 2 report we can review? Also any FedRAMP or HIPAA BAAs?
01:40 Jared: We have SOC 2 Type II report and can share the attestation with your security team. For HIPAA, we do offer a BAA for enterprise Private deployments — we'll loop Legal and Security to get the paperwork started.
01:53 Emily: Great. Timeline wise, we need access to a sandbox environment and a small quota to run a 2k docs pilot. What's typical lead time?
02:02 Priya: For Hosted onboarding it's usually immediate; for Dedicated it's 5-10 business days for capacity provisioning; for Private there's network work — usually 2-3 weeks for initial setup depending on your network team. For a pilot we can often spin up a hosted trial with restricted retention so you can start ingesting data while Private gets provisioned in parallel.
02:23 Sofia: That hybrid approach sounds good. But we need to validate that data in hosted trial won't be retained — what's the retention policy?
02:30 Marcus: For trials we can configure a short retention window and disable training/retention hooks. We'll include the exact retention policy in the security pack. Note: auto-transcription sometimes mislabels things, sorry 'transcription' I mean 'training'.
02:45 Emily: ha, yeah, we want zero training and short logs. Also can you confirm SSO? We use Okta and need SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning.
02:53 Priya: Okta SAML + SCIM is supported. We'll send the SSO guide and a template metadata file. Marcus will also help with role-based access configuration so you can lock down project-level access.
03:06 Raj: Networking question — do you require VPC peering or can we use private link? We prefer PrivateLink due to firewall constraints.
03:14 Marcus: We support both VPC peering and PrivateLink depending on region and deployment. For Private we typically do an ingress endpoint and mTLS, or PrivateLink if you prefer. We'll capture requirements in the technical deep dive.
03:30 Emily: For success criteria for the pilot, we want: 1) <10% error in summary quality compared to human baseline, 2) average inference latency under 400ms for short notes, 3) no PHI leakage in logs. Is that feasible?
03:46 Jared: Those are reasonable goals. We'll work with you to define sampling and evaluation methods and plug into Redwood Optimize to track quality/regressions. Marcus will help design the eval harness.
03:58 Marcus: Yep we'll set up an eval suite, will ask for labeled subset for ground truth. Also note that latency will depend on model choice and batching config; we can recommend model and quantization profile for your throughput target.
04:12 Sofia: Speaking of model choice, are you running open models or proprietary ones? We had another vendor pushing closed models which raised questions about auditing.
04:20 Jared: Redwood supports curated open models and also partner models; everything we serve has performance profiles. For Private deployments you can bring your own model binaries or use our curated ones; we log model versions and have rollout controls.
04:34 Raj: Cool. Any known customers in healthcare doing similar pilots?
04:40 Priya: We have a few health system pilots — I can share anonymized case studies and a short checklist showing typical timelines and pitfalls.
04:48 Emily: Please do. Also can you share pricing? We might need a cost estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private for the pilot and for 6 month production run.
04:58 Jared: Absolutely — I'll send a pricing addendum with cost per-token for Hosted, commit tiers for Dedicated, and an estimate for Private (one-time infra + monthly support). We'll call out egress and storage too.
05:12 Sofia: Security docs — we'll want SOC2, pen test summary, encryption-at-rest details, and network architecture example. Who will own delivering those?
05:20 Marcus: We'll package a security binder — Priya will deliver the docs and Jared will copy Legal. Expect SOC2 and pen test summary; for deeper architecture we'll schedule a follow-up with our security engineer.
05:32 Emily: OK next steps recap?
05:36 Priya: I'll share onboarding checklist, SSO/SCIM guide, and security binder by Monday 2027-09-06.
05:42 Marcus: I'll schedule the technical deep dive for next week, target 2027-09-09, and prepare VPC/PrivateLink options.
05:48 Jared: I'll send pricing and Dedicated vs Hosted matrix by 2027-09-04 and open the BAA thread with Legal.
05:54 Emily: We'll confirm pilot datasets and PHI scope by 2027-09-08 and get back on the access/okta side.
06:00 Raj: Sounds good thanks everyone.
06:04 Jared: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with the links to the doc repo and checklist.

Notes/Links referenced: 
- Onboarding checklist (link to Redwood onboarding doc)
- Security pack (SOC2, pen test summary, encryption notes)
- SSO/SCIM guide (Okta metadata template)
- Pricing addendum (to be sent)

End of transcript.
